title: Tapping Product Consistency & Trust Hardening
objective: Controlled terminology-consistency pass across the tapping product chain (Atlas, Tap-Type Guide, Workflow, Comparison, Evidence, Tap Drill Calculator overlap). No new pages, no new data, no knowledge-layer or T3 projection changes.

t11_correction.title: Fix provenance validator check #8 (validator-quality defect, found after the original T11 pass)
t11_correction.root_cause: Check #8 in scripts/validators/validate-tapping-terminology.js was intended to enforce 'no fabricated provenance fallback,' but its actual condition was `!isTemplateCode && !approvedFallbacks.includes(value) && value === ""` -- the trailing `value === ""` meant only an EMPTY rendered value could ever fail the check. An arbitrary non-empty fabricated string (e.g. 'fabricated-source') satisfied `value === ""` as false and therefore passed silently, regardless of the other two conditions. The check did not enforce what its name and comment claimed.
t11_correction.correction_summary: Check #8 was rewritten to resolve every provenance value each product actually exposes and compare it against the authoritative projection data, rather than pattern-matching for emptiness: (a) Atlas's statically-rendered Source dataset/record/field/Cross-check per card are matched to the corresponding tapping-profiles.json row by designation and compared field-by-field; (b) Tap-Type Guide's statically-rendered per-fact 'source: ...' text is matched to the corresponding tap-types.json note by fact text and compared; (c) since Workflow and Evidence render provenance client-side from js/tapping-workflow-data.js rather than resolving it into static HTML, that data file's embedded tap_drill.provenance and tap-type note fields are parsed and compared directly against tapping-profiles.json/tap-types.json, which validates the actual data those products will render without needing to execute a browser; (d) Evidence's specific fallback expressions (e.g. `prov.source_dataset || "..."`) are checked to confirm they are still genuine property-access expressions using one of the three approved fallback literals, not a hardcoded replacement. A value is now accepted only if it exactly matches the projection-backed value, or if the projection has no value for that field AND the rendered value is one of the three approved fallback strings.
distinguishes_three_cases: A. A resolved provenance value that exactly matches the projection-backed source data -- accepted.
B. An explicitly approved fallback string, used only when the projection genuinely has no value for that field -- accepted.

C. Client-side/template code (JS property-access expressions) that is not itself a resolved value -- not scanned as if it were a resolved value; instead the underlying data file it will resolve against (js/tapping-workflow-data.js) is validated directly.

known_issue.description: T10 corrected 'ISO 2306 metric convention' to 'Metric drill convention' in its own implementation (generate-tapping-evidence.js), but the older wording remained in the T4 Atlas generator and T8 Workflow generator.
found_in: scripts/generators/generate-tapping-workflow.js:394 (isoAlternativeCell, pre-fix) -- T9 comparison table, metric-record 'Not applicable' cell
known_issue.correction_summary: HTML/UI-facing occurrences in the Atlas and Workflow generators now say 'Metric drill convention' (or reference 'the metric drill convention' in prose), matching T10's baseline, because only 9 of 14 metric records have projection-backed ISO 2306 cross-verification (tap_drill.provenance.cross_check present); the remaining 5 are source-bound. The CSV's 'primary_drill_convention' column is a protected, frozen artifact under the T11 regression rule and intentionally still reads 'ISO 2306 metric convention' -- this is a documented, deliberate exception, not an oversight, achieved by splitting the shared label function into a display-only function and a CSV-only function that preserves the original text exactly.

additional_inconsistencies_found.description: Atlas and Workflow's single-record view labeled the data_quality.record_status field 'Overall profile status', while Evidence (T10 baseline) and Workflow's own T9 comparison table both used 'Overall record status' for the identical field -- an inconsistency both across products and within tools/tapping-workflow.html itself.
additional_inconsistencies_found.correction: Changed 'Overall profile status' to 'Overall record status' in generate-tapping-atlas.js and generate-tapping-workflow.js (single-record view) to match T10's baseline and the comparison table's own existing label.

additional_inconsistencies_found.description: Section 8 freezes the tap-type classification labels in plural form ('Manufacturing characteristics', 'Typical applications', 'Manufacturer-specific recommendations'). The Atlas, Tap-Type Guide, and Workflow generators rendered these as SECTION HEADINGS in singular form ('Manufacturing characteristic', 'Typical application', 'Manufacturer-specific recommendation'), while Evidence (T10 baseline) already used the plural heading form specified in section 8. Evidence's separate singular usage in its per-fact 'evidence kind: X' inline annotation is grammatically correct and was left untouched.
additional_inconsistencies_found.correction: Changed the three SECTION HEADING calls (not the per-fact inline mentions) in generate-tapping-atlas.js, generate-tap-type-guide.js, and generate-tapping-workflow.js to plural form, matching section 8's frozen spec and the Evidence baseline.

csv_protected_artifact_exception.reason: Section 14 lists downloads/tapping-atlas.csv as a file T11 must not alter. The generator's driveConventionLabel function was split into a display-only function (used for the HTML card) and a new csvDriveConventionLabel function (used only in renderCsv) that reproduces the original 'ISO 2306 metric convention' / 'US customary drill convention' text verbatim, so the CSV output is provably byte-identical across the change.

terminology_matrix.note: No plural form applies; identical label everywhere.

Workflow, Comparison, and Evidence all use the frozen sentence verbatim: 'Thread engagement calculation is not currently available in BoltLab's verified dataset.' Atlas uses a longer, more detailed radial/axial explanation (accurate to the projection's engagement.radial.calculation_status='calculable' / engagement.axial.calculation_status='not_calculable' fields) established in T4/T7 and reaffirmed in its own FAQ. Reviewed and intentionally left as-is -- see Section 9 finding below.

'Source dataset' / 'Source record' / 'Source field' labels identical in both products that render provenance. Workflow and Tap-Type Guide do not expose provenance blocks, which is acceptable per section 7.

Evidence structurally separates 'Provenance' and 'Cross-verification' into two labeled blocks; Atlas includes an additional 'Cross-check' line item within its single 'Data provenance' list. Both keep original-source and cross-check evidence distinctly labeled (never collapsed into one 'source'); the structural difference is an acceptable product-context variation, not a terminology collapse. Reviewed, no change required.

All standards designations shown on tapping-atlas.html records verified present in the tapping-profiles projection (validate-tapping-terminology.js check 9). No standard is displayed without projection backing.

intentionally_unchanged.item: Engagement-language phrasing difference between Atlas (radial/axial detailed explanation) and Workflow/Evidence/Comparison (short frozen sentence)
intentionally_unchanged.reason: Both are individually accurate to the projection's engagement.radial/axial fields. The short sentence is the section-9 frozen authoritative sentence, quoted verbatim in Workflow/Evidence/Comparison. Atlas's longer form is an established, accurate elaboration from T4/T7, not part of the section-2 known issue. Forcing identical wording would either delete accurate nuance from Atlas or expand Workflow/Evidence beyond a terminology-only fix -- out of T11 scope per section 13's 'only make changes when there is a real semantic inconsistency' rule.

intentionally_unchanged.item: Atlas's flat 'Data provenance' list (including 'Cross-check' as one more line item) vs. Evidence's structurally separate 'Provenance' and 'Cross-verification' sections
intentionally_unchanged.reason: Section 6 permits a product not to expose the same structural depth of cross-verification detail as another, and both products already keep the concepts distinctly labeled rather than collapsed into one 'source'. Adding a two-section split to Atlas, or a 'Cited source/standard' line reproducing Evidence's prov.source rendering, would be adding new UI structure, not a terminology correction -- out of scope per section 13 and the 'do not add new claims solely to make every product identical' rule in section 6.

intentionally_unchanged.item: downloads/tapping-atlas.csv 'primary_drill_convention' column retains 'ISO 2306 metric convention' text
intentionally_unchanged.reason: Explicit T11 regression-rule protection (section 14): the CSV must not be altered. See csv_protected_artifact_exception above.
